title: The Truth About "Trading Gurus" From a Hedge Fund Manager
summary: A scam-investigation channel interviews a quant hedge fund manager on why trading gurus' claimed returns are impossible, why profitable strategies are not sold, hidden costs of 'free' trading, options leverage, candlestick backtests and realistic expectations for small accounts.

assertions.quote: if you take two percent a day that would turn into about i don't know 140 000 percent a year roughly

verdicts.note: Compounding arithmetic; no documented investor has sustained anything close.

assertions.quote: the nature of those kinds of strategies as i've said they're usually not scalable and so you keep them as a secret

verdicts.note: Quant funds routinely cap capacity and guard strategies; selling a capacity-limited edge destroys it, which makes advertised strategies suspect.

assertions.quote: give signals to their audience who then rushes out and buys the thing and they sell it on

verdicts.note: Regulators have charged influencers and newsletter operators for exactly this; event studies show audience-driven price spikes.

assertions.quote: if they don't charge you a commission but route your your trades to you know a high frequency trader they've been well compensated for this

verdicts.note: Payment for order flow is documented; whether execution is worse than a commission model is contested, with some studies finding price improvement.

Zero-commission brokers are paid for order flow by wholesalers, and the true trading cost (12.3% average quoted spread on the weekly options retail prefers) is masked by zero commissions; indirect spread costs of $4.13bn dwarf $0.8bn of direct commissions.

Wholesalers pay commission-free brokerages for the orders routed to them (payment for order flow), giving brokers an incentive to push trading in wider-spread assets; in Q2 2021 US brokerages received $284.4m of PFOF for stock orders and $581.2m for options.

Brokers are paid by wholesalers for routing retail orders, but the cost differs by asset: in stocks wholesaler routing benefits retail with smaller spreads than the exchanges, while in options it harms them, PFOF-paying market makers being causally associated with wider spreads (quasi-random DMM assignments).

assertions.quote: the day traders who do well one year even two years typically it's only a minor indication of how well they'll do
he kind of glosses over that if it moves against you at all that you will materially uh you know lose everything

verdicts.note: Bought options cap loss at the premium but expire worthless often; written or margined positions can exceed invested capital.

For leveraged CFDs (not options) ESMA finds high leverage makes positions sensitive to small price moves and investors risk losing all or more than their initial margin; a bought option cannot lose more than its premium.

assertions.quote: many of them that were sort of supposed to be bullish signals were were bearish signals

verdicts.note: Academic tests of candlestick signals on major indices find no profitable predictive power after costs.

assertions.quote: it's all short-term gains right which is taxed at a terrible rate

verdicts.note: Spreads, fees and ordinary-income tax treatment of short-term gains are structural.
Trading costs more than triple day traders' losses, from 7 bps gross to 23.9 bps net per day; the tax-rate part of the claim is not examined.

assertions.quote: you don't just lose some of your savings you can also sort of harm your career

verdicts.note: Opportunity cost and resume gaps are real; most who try full-time trading return to employment.
Only 8 of 1,551 persistent day traders (0.5%) earned more than a bank teller's starting salary, so for nearly all, trading income would not replace the wage given up.

assertions.quote: your return is 20 000 a year you need to get a job

verdicts.note: Top long-run investor records are around twenty percent a year; applied to typical retail capital that is below median wages.
99.5% of persistent day traders earned less than a bank teller; the top eight beat that wage only with daily profit standard deviations of US$632-3,308, and account size is not examined.

assertions.quote: if you're buying stuff we'll say cheaply from a manufacturer and selling it to someone else that's a shop that's called a shop

verdicts.note: Marketplace sellers face fee stacks, price competition and platform control; survey data show most small sellers earn little.

Empire's model bought items from other retailers after a sale and resold them on Amazon 'for a small profit taking advantage of the price difference'; confirms thin margins for this arbitrage-dropship variant only.

assertions.quote: if there was something easy out there someone else would grab it
